Enhanced due diligence mandatory for any Politically Exposed Person (PEP) under FINTRAC regulations, with senior management approval required for high-risk relationships.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online portal — https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French is mandatory in the corporate name under the Charter of the French Language (CQLR c C-11); the name must include a French legal designation or an accepted French descriptor unless an approved bilingual form is registered. Non-Latin script words must be transliterated into the Latin alphabet in the official registration, and the registered French form prevails for all formal legal acts.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon name rejection, the applicant may file a written reconsideration request with the Registraire des entreprises within 30 days of the notice, attaching evidence of distinctiveness and French-language compliance. If rejected again, an appeal to the Administrative Tribunal of Quebec (Tribunal administratif du Quebec) must be lodged within 60 days from the final refusal, with the corporation or proposed corporation represented by a Quebec-licensed lawyer.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Not permissible for an equity crowdfunding portal as the primary registered office. The Autorite des marches financiers and FINTRAC expect a physical operational presence in Quebec for records, board meetings, compliance functions, and regulatory inspections; a virtual office can only serve as supplemental back-office accommodation if a physical registered office and physical records location are separately maintained.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 85% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection by the Autorite des marches financiers or FINTRAC within the first 12 months of active portal operation, given the high-risk securities intermediation classification.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Draft and Submit Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare Articles of Incorporation detailing corporate name, registered office address, authorized share capital, names and addresses of directors and officers; obtain signatures; submit electronically to REDAQ with payment of CAD 300 filing fee and any required supporting documents such as proof of address.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried for incompleteness or errors, submit a cure within 10 business days by amending the filing

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Obtain Certificate of Incorporation and Initial Compliance

step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If processing exceeds SLA or is delayed, contact REDAQ support to expedite or file a formal complaint

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Revenu Québec (RQ) for provincial taxes and Canada Revenue Agency (CRA) for federal taxes; portals: www.revenuquebec.ca and www.canada.ca/cra
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Obtain Business Number (BN) from CRA via online portal or Form RC1; register with Revenu Québec for provincial taxes including QST if annual taxable supplies exceed threshold
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box elections in Canada; tax classification fixed by legal structure as corporation (entity-level taxation); hybrid mismatch rules under ATIR may apply in limited cases

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Real-time digital reporting and electronic invoicing mandated for businesses above thresholds; API integration with RQ portal for fiscal clearance and digital stamping

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: 0% rate for exports of goods and services performed outside Canada; must demonstrate export occurred and ownership transferred to non-resident
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Bill of Lading or equivalent proof of export, evidence of service performance outside Canada
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Non-exported supplies trigger retrospective tax assessment plus interest; penalties up to 50% of tax or higher for fraudulent claims; clawback of input tax credits and potential criminal sanctions

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada); however, Canada maintains no dedicated foreign-exchange control authority or exchange-control licensing regime. FX administration is limited to FINTRAC cross-border reporting, OSFI prudential oversight, and CRA Part XIII withholding administration.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII jurisdiction: both current-account and capital-account transactions are fully convertible and unrestricted. Profit remittance is immediate and unlicensed; a dividend paid by a Quebec corporation attracts a 25% statutory Part XIII withholding tax, reducible to 15% or 5% under an applicable treaty provided the non-resident beneficial owner files the required CRA treaty form. No central-bank or Finance Department pre-approval is required for inbound or outbound transfers.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada abolished exchange controls in 1951; there is no statutory timeline, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no obligation to repatriate export proceeds to Canada. Exporters may retain 100% of foreign-currency receipts in Canada or abroad. Only FINTRAC reporting obligations apply to cross-border transfers of CAD 10,000 or more, and corporate accounts must comply with CDR/IFRS record-keeping.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium. Canada has no EU-style EMI passport. A foreign digital EMI may not lawfully hold client funds in escrow or accept deposits in Canada without a Canadian bank or trust charter. EMIs may function only as payment-order gateways routing to a CDIC-member institution under the Retail Payment Activities Act registration, if applicable. A portal relying on an unregulated offshore EMI will face account termination by Tier-1 banks.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Certain AMF-regulated portals may be onboarded remotely, but Quebec-based commercial bankers generally require at least one in-person KYC interview of the ultimate beneficial owner and the AML compliance officer at a Montreal or Quebec City branch. A remote video interview is accepted when the entity has a physical Quebec address, an executed AMF registration, and two independent identity documents. Non-resident directors may be approved remotely with notarized corporate resolutions and a bank reference from an existing institution.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk crowdfunding classification triggered by ISIC 6499 / NAICS 523999 and exposure to unregulated retail investors.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: AMF crowdfunding portal registration or restricted-dealer registration, executed escrow and trust-account agreement, FINTRAC-specific AML/CFT compliance program, Board resolution on investor acceptance, sample redacted investor EDD file, and evidence that investor funds pass only through a CDIC-member bank.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial ownership, foreign economic exposure, or sanctions-relevant investor base.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Certified passports, permanent-residence certificate, enhanced sanctions-screening output, six months of primary bank statements, notarized source-of-funds declaration, and independent accountant's financial due-diligence letter.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Opaque ownership chain, nominee arrangements, or inability to identify owners controlling 25% or more of the portal.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current federal and Registraire des entreprises extracts, certificates of incorporation and articles, full capitalization table, notarized beneficial-ownership declaration, and audited shareholder register.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Perceived regulatory ambiguity as to whether the portal receives funds in trust without a recognized dealer licence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Quebec securities lawyer legal opinion on the applicable crowdfunding prospectus exemption, executed portal-issuer agreement delineating intermediary duties, evidence that funds are held in a named escrow suspens account, and an unqualified audit opinion with no fiduciary liabilities.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Investor subscriptions are cleared by ACH pre-authorized debit via Payments Canada ACSS or by high-value CAD/USD wire via LVTS or SWIFT MT103 into the Quebec-based segregated escrow account held at a CDIC-member bank. MT103 narrative must identify the offering and state purpose code EQUI. FINTRAC EFT reports are mandatory for transfers of CAD 10,000 or more. Investor funds must not be routed to any non-Canadian account prior to escrow release.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Settlement disbursements use: domestic CAD wires through LVTS; cross-border SWIFT MT103 payments with invoice or security-settlement references; and commercial letters of credit under MT700/MT707 for trade settlements. ACH credits via ACSS are permitted only for low-value recurring disbursements to verified issuer accounts. Third-party nominee payouts are prohibited; each disbursement must match the executed issuer funding agreement.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Deliverable CAD/USD FX forwards of up to 24 months documented under an ISDA 2002 master agreement or a bank treasury master agreement.
Cross-currency swaps on CAD/USD with ISDA documentation and OSFI-compliant margin/collateral arrangements.
OTC vanilla FX options for hedging committed subscription and trade settlement flows.

Non-deliverable forwards in third-currency restricted markets (e.g., CNY, INR, BRL) for outbound trade settlements, executed offshore with a regulated counterparty; NDFs in CAD are not standard because CAD is fully convertible.
FX swaps for temporary cross-currency liquidity equalization, subject to the bank's dealing-room limits.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Return under the Canada Business Corporations Act (Form 22; federal annual return, if the corporation is incorporated under the CBCA and carries on business in Quebec through extra-provincial registration)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada – Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada (ISED)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 60 days after each anniversary of the federal incorporation date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing penalty of approximately CAD 100; repeated failure for two consecutive years exposes the corporation to a notice of administrative dissolution by the Director followed by certificate of dissolution.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual Updating Declaration (Déclaration de mise à jour annuelle) for the Quebec enterprise registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than the anniversary date of the enterprise registration in the REQ; for federal corporations registered extra-provincially in Quebec, the same anniversary rule applies to the REQ record.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Default triggers a registraire notice; if unaddressed within about 30 days, the registration is cancelled (radiation) and the corporation loses its standing to operate in Quebec. Reinstatement requires an order or application and payment of all unpaid dues and penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual audited financial statements and regulatory filings required for the equity crowdfunding portal licence
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 90 days after each fiscal year-end, or such other period specified by the AMF in the portal's registration order.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-receipt can lead to suspension or revocation of the crowdfunding registration, a cease-trade order, and administrative monetary penalties under the Quebec Securities Act.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A private CBCA/QBCA corporation is not required to appoint an auditor solely by size if all shareholders waive the audit. A mandatory independent audit is triggered when: (i) the corporation is a reporting issuer or 'distributing' corporation under Canadian securities law; (ii) shareholders who collectively hold at least 5% of the voting shares requisition an audit; (iii) the articles, by-laws, a unanimous shareholder agreement, or a court order requires an audit; or (iv) the AMF imposes audited financial statements as a condition of the equity crowdfunding portal registration or prospectus exemption.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: IFRS for public/reporting issuers; Part II of the CPA Canada Handbook - Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises (ASPE) for Canadian private corporations; the AMF may require statements prepared in accordance with Canadian GAAP adapted to IFRS or ASPE.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: CBCA and QBCA require every corporation to maintain a Register of Individuals with Significant Control (RISC). The register must be updated within 15 days after the corporation learns of a change in significant control, and prescribed persons may inspect it at the registered office. No separate annual UBO renewal is filed with the registrar; instead, the corporation confirms the register's accuracy during its annual updating declaration/return process and must keep all share-transfer and UBO changes recorded.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 200 – USD 900 per year for a commercial registered office or registered agent in Quebec; using an in-house registered office eliminates the agent fee but must still satisfy the mandatory statutory availability hours and mailing-address requirements.
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 6,000 – USD 20,000 per year for a small-to-mid-size private equity-crowdfunding portal, depending on transaction volume, escrow balances, revenue recognition, and AMF regulatory review requirements.

stage_6.entry_description: Legal name, business number (BN), income tax account number, mailing address, and taxation year-end date.
stage_6.non_resident_entry_guidance: A non-resident corporation files the T2 only if it carries on business in Canada, disposes of taxable Canadian property, or has a taxable Canadian-source event; state the Canadian agent/branch address and complete Schedule 91 (provincial allocation).
